Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded by $y=-x$ and $y=2-{x}^{2},$ shown above?

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*
feedback.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the intersection points between the two graphs occur when $x=-1$ and $x=2.$ So these will be our limits of integration.

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/9e6e1147d95c65465c802e8bfad5c4ac285dc9716d098452c41bdd6caed5b9ca.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=-x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=2-{x}^{2}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}[\,(2-{x}^{2})-(-x)\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}(-{x}^{2}+x+2)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
